title: LTS channel governance and automated upgrade verifier
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define a cross-surface governance model for long-term-support (LTS) channels and implement an automated preflight verifier that validates upgrades across runtime, API, SDKs, and Console before cohort rollouts. The verifier should enforce semantic compatibility, run contract and e2e inference tests, verify rollback readiness, and surface a single pass/fail decision with a human-readable report for release engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Governance matrix published that maps LTS lane guarantees to component-level contracts (runtime, API, SDK, console)
Automated verifier runs as part of pre-rollout and produces a reproducible report in under 30 minutes for standard release candidate

Verifier includes: API contract tests, SDK integration smoke tests for top-3 languages, runtime binary/quantization compatibility checks, console migration flag validation, and latency/regression thresholds
Rollout gating rule implemented in rollout orchestration: a failed verifier blocks canary cohort expansion and triggers automated rollback plan creation
Documentation (confluence) and runbook updated; at least one dry-run conducted with dedicated capacity and lessons captured
implementation_plan: Draft governance matrix and publish for review with PM/Design/SRE
Prototype verifier as a kubernetes job that executes staged checks against a release candidate cluster

Instrument existing test suites: add API contract runner (wiremock + pact), add SDK language smoke runners (python, go, typescript), add runtime binary compatibility script (model load + kv-cache smoke), add quantization profile validator
Create gating integration with rollout service: contributor submits release candidate -> verifier job runs -> gate result posted to release UI and rollout API
Run two dry-runs on internal staging with simulated customer traffic and iterate on failure modes
Hand-off runbook and monitor for 2 subsequent LTS releases to validate process stability
progress_updates: 2026-02-27: Kickoff meeting with Release Eng, Runtime, SDK, Console leads. Agreed on scope and initial success metrics.
2026-03-03: Draft governance matrix shared (link below). Early feedback: Console team requests explicit feature-flag verification for UI compatibility.
2026-03-08: Prototype verifier container created (repo: github.com/redwood/release-verifier). Basic API contract test and python SDK smoke test wired up.
2026-03-10: Performance SLA added to acceptance criteria: detect >10% median latency regression on standard demo prompts and fail the verifier.
2026-03-12: Security review requested. SRE requested ability to run verifier in VPC-proxied mode for Private deployments. Working on credentials passthrough design.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Verifier runtime grows and delays rollouts. Mitigation: stage checks so quick boolean failures (contract, binary load) run first; heavy e2e workloads run asynchronously but block expansion until complete.
Risk: False-positives from flaky tests. Mitigation: stabilize harnesses, add retry/backoff and require 2 consecutive failures to block rollout.
Risk: Private/VPC environments cannot access verifier artifacts. Mitigation: design verifier to run in-customer or in a proxy mode with artifact bundling and signed manifests.
Risk: SDK language coverage gaps. Mitigation: prioritize top-3 languages for LTS contracts and add others to backlog with telemetry-driven prioritization.
